purpose: Declared INTENT for each mutant, frozen in G0 so later gates check the map against a stated expectation rather than against whatever the map happens to say. These are expectations, not results: SM1-G1 checks the declaration_id column, SM1-G2 checks abi_equal and body_equal.
subject: the declaration under observation in each mutant; unrelated-mutation cases observe 'topLevel' precisely because it was NOT touched

columns.declaration_id_stable: the SUBJECT's DECLARATION_ID must be unchanged from base
columns.abi_equal: the SUBJECT's ABI_FINGERPRINT must equal base
columns.body_equal: the SUBJECT's BODY_FINGERPRINT must equal base

mutants.subject: corpus.app::topLevel
mutants.note: the load-bearing case: a body change must NOT move the declaration id, or the map cannot say 'same declaration, new implementation'

mutants.subject: corpus.app::topLevel
mutants.note: body is textually identical; only the return type moved. If the map reports abi_equal here it is deriving ABI from the body.

mutants.subject: corpus.app::Shape.area
mutants.note: also inside the ROADMAP P2 refusal boundary; the map must state the refusal rather than mis-classify

mutants.subject: corpus.app::topLevel
mutants.note: the anti-order-dependence case: an index- or offset-derived identity fails here

mutants.subject: corpus.app::Shape.area
mutants.dimension: field added to the owning class
mutants.note: the METHOD is unchanged. Whether the owning class's layout change makes the method unsafe to reuse is a SEPARATE question owned by SM1-G5, and must not be smuggled into the fingerprints.

mutants.subject: corpus.app::usesPrivate
mutants.dimension: private body changed in a DIFFERENT library
mutants.note: corpus.helper::_privateHelper and corpus.app::_privateHelper share a simple name across privacy domains; a map that confuses them will report app's caller as changed

dimensions_owned_elsewhere.why: a contract-level withholding, not a source mutation
